Before selecting or serving a file, file_response resolves the request document and its root document, then applies has_perms_owner_aware to the root document with the view_document permission. Under the stated premises, the caller is not the root owner and has no object view grant, so this owner-aware check fails and returns HttpResponseForbidden. The source therefore denies this scenario at the declared-entry boundary and aligns with the accepted policy requiring the root-document check before serving any selected version. def has_perms_owner_aware(user, perms, obj):
    """
    Legacy slow path (guardian-backed) single-object permission check.

    The queryset-filtering side of this migrated onto
    ``PermittedObjectsFilter``/``permitted_object_ids()``, but this
    single-object check still has many production callers. Several callers
    remain across ``documents/``, ``paperless_mail/``, and ``paperless_ai/``
    -- grep for this function name before removing it.
    """
    checker = ObjectPermissionChecker(user)
    return obj.owner is None or obj.owner == user or checker.has_perm(perms, obj)

binding.statement: file_response resolves the requested document's root document and the authorization check is applied to that root document, not directly to the requested version document.
After authorization, the effective file document is either the request document for the no-version child path or a document resolved for the requested version from root_doc.

control.statement: The decisive control calls has_perms_owner_aware for view_document on root_doc and returns HttpResponseForbidden when it fails.

effect.statement: Only after the authorization gate succeeds does file_response pass the selected file_doc to serve_file, which serves that document's archive or source file.
